claims.statement: useGame opens a single useStream on the `chess` assistant per game, and every submit carries configurable set to exactly the ChessContext fields of the game's record (DEFAULT_CONTEXT only as a stand-in when there is no record), run_name chess-web with tag web, metadata surface web, and multitaskStrategy reject.

The web UI stores the current game's thread id in the `thread` URL query parameter via history.replaceState; when useStream reports a new thread id and the hook is still mounted, it binds the id and writes it to the URL, and the browser stores nothing per game because the game's setup lives in the thread.

On load, App seats the thread found in the URL with no chosen record so its setup comes from the thread; a new game or rematch clears the URL thread and creates a seat with a higher number and a chosen side and context (a rematch swaps sides and keeps the context), remounting the keyed Table so useStream starts a fresh thread, and a seat where the human plays Black auto-sends `go` once on mount guarded by a ref.

Human commands get message ids memoized per hook instance (one game) by the key ply:content, deliberately excluding the thread id because a new game's first command is sent before a thread exists, so a resend of the same command at the same position reuses the id, which the server treats as a no-op for already-consumed ids.

useGame's play sends the UCI move as a human message with an optimistic pendingMove shown until the submit settles, start sends `go`, and retry submits empty input to resume a pending turn because a fresh `go` is rejected while a turn is pending.

The Table locks the board when the game has no record or has not finished loading, when viewing an earlier ply, while loading, after the game ends, while a turn is pending, or while an optimistic move is in flight, and it swallows the SDK's 'a run is already in flight' rejection while surfacing other submit errors.

Auth failures (HTTP status 401/403, or SDK request messages anchored at the start as HTTP/Protocol/Thread state request failures with 401/403, so a model provider's 401 inside a run does not match) show a banner directing the user to Settings, where the only app-level setting is the LangSmith API key stored under langchain-chess:app and passed to useStream.

Pressing Play in the New game dialog first checks the API key by POSTing to /assistants/search: 401/403 is 'missing' without a key and 'rejected' with one, a network failure is 'unreachable', and anything else is ok; the game starts only on ok and only if the picks on screen are unchanged and still playable, and a late answer after unmount is ignored.

matchupOf derives the policy from the dialog picks (hybrid with both System 1 and an LLM, otherwise systemone or llm), rejects picking neither, an empty custom model spec, or an LLM game with memory summarize while the model's limit is being checked or could not be checked, downgrades summarize to none for a model without a known limit, and fills the unused model field with its default; a Random side is resolved once when Play is pressed.
With no game on screen the New game dialog cannot be closed, and opening Settings from it preserves the unsaved picks as a draft that is restored on return.

The server exposes GET /ui/config returning the graph id, JSON schema and defaults of ChessContext, but the web client does not fetch it; context types, ranges and defaults are hand-mirrored in chess-ui types.ts and web settings.ts CONTEXT_CHECKS.

localStorage holds only the last New game setup and the API key; stored setups are untrusted, with each field and knob that fails validation falling back to its default individually, the removed memory value `full` mapped to `summarize`, and the legacy global settings blob migrated only while the newer keys are absent.

apiUrl uses VITE_API_URL if set, otherwise http://localhost:2024 in dev, otherwise the page origin; the production web build uses base /ui/ and outputs into the Python server package's static directory, which the server mounts at /ui.

packages/chess-ui is a private package whose exports point at TypeScript source (src/index.ts, styles.css, testing.ts) with no build step, so consuming apps compile it and must include its source in their Tailwind content globs and import its stylesheet.

chess-ui's ChessValues lists the only thread channels a UI may read (messages, start_fen, moves, plies, turns, outcome, error, and the optional setup); positions are rebuilt client-side by replaying moves, stopping silently at the first move chess.js rejects because the server is authoritative.

liveAnalysis returns the latest AI text after the current turn opened (or after the last human message), skipping AI messages already committed as a ply's message, so a previous move's analysis is never shown as live.

apps/review is built as a single dependency-free CommonJS bundle exporting render(data, container, metadata) for the LangSmith custom-app sandbox, with code splitting disabled and NODE_ENV defined as production outside Vitest; render creates the root, stylesheet and api dependencies once and re-renders in place so host updates do not reset loads.

The review app talks only to the LangSmith API through window.langsmith.call: it lists projects, queries threads by project and time window in pages of 20, then fetches the threads' last root runs and game_review feedback in parallel and joins them into games.

reviewsByRun only considers feedback with key game_review, a run_id, and feedback_source metadata grader 'lcchess grade' (other feedback under the key is ignored), and parseReview classifies it as graded only for a complete version-1 review with well-formed evals and ply grades and one eval per position, otherwise as invalid with the first problem found.

A review game's values are the last root run's outputs only when they validate as a game record (a UCI moves array plus well-shaped optional start_fen, plies, turns and outcome); otherwise the app shows 'No game record', and ungraded games show a hint to run lcchess grade --thread.

GameView marks move-list entries with graded quality, draws the played move and the engine's differing best move as arrows, shows an eval bar, grade card and eval graph from a graded review's per-position evals, and shows a 'Review unreadable' banner suggesting a forced regrade for invalid reviews.
The review App tags each loaded games page with its project and since query so a stale response is never displayed for a newer query.

The pnpm workspace contains apps/web, apps/review and packages/*, with shared dependency versions pinned in a catalog (vite aliased to vite-plus-core) and referenced as catalog: so packages cannot drift.

Lint and format are configured only in the root vite.config.ts because Vite+ ignores nested lint/fmt blocks; lint is type-aware oxlint with rules-of-hooks and prefer-vite-plus-imports, and formatting ignores apps/server, libs and openwiki.

The web and review apps run jsdom Vitest over tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} with 100% line, function, branch and statement coverage thresholds; the review app writes coverage outside its directory because langsmith apps push ignores .gitignore.

Web tests replace useStream with a shared fake that records options, supports per-thread overrides and simulates thread-load outcomes, a separate suite exercises useGame on the real SDK over stubbed fetch, and App accepts injectable random, checkKey and modelLimit so tests are deterministic without a server.

The New game dialog asks the server for the chosen LLM's input limit via GET /ui/model-limit (debounced 300 ms, sending x-api-key when set); a numeric max_input_tokens is known, null means the model has no known limit, and non-OK responses, malformed bodies and network errors are 'failed'; the summarize option is disabled only for models with no known limit, a failed check blocks a summarize game with a Retry, and late answers for a no-longer-selected model are ignored.

The server's GameSetupMiddleware records the run's resolved ChessContext in a public, client-unwritable `setup` state channel only in the run that opened the game's first turn (both before and after the agent so failed or game-ending first turns still get it), never overwrites it, and never adds it to threads created before it existed.

The web UI continues a game from its thread: gameOf takes the context from the thread's `setup` only when every ChessContext key is present and valid (recordedContext), falls back to a new game's chosen context before its first turn is recorded, and otherwise yields no record so the game is view-only.

The human's side of a continued game is derived from the thread: the side of the last external ply, else the opposite of whoever played ply 0, else the picked side, else the side not to move in the start position.

useGame tracks each thread load by the SDK hydration promise as loading, missing (a clean load for a thread id that binds no thread), failed (rejected load) or ready, ignores superseded loads settling late, and the Table shows a Reload banner for failed loads and a not-on-server banner for missing threads while keeping the board locked.

The web app tolerates blocked localStorage: browserStorage returns null when storage access throws, writers report whether a save landed, and App shows a 'This browser isn't saving' banner when storage is blocked or a save fails.
The review app marks a graded review invalid when its ply UCIs do not match the game's moves, so evaluations are never drawn against a different move sequence.
